bw-5g1x.title: Coverage: overcast on the western A2
bw-5g1x.summary: The western part of the A2 has overcast coverage, which makes it recognisable.

bw-6gap.title: City: lone hill with radio antennas on north
bw-6gap.summary: Francistown often shows a lone hill with radio antennas on its north side, which tells it from the capital. Serowe has a similar hill, but with taller red-and-white striped towers and a flat top.

bw-84qU.title: Coverage: rural dirt tracks, orange-red dirt
bw-84qU.summary: Near the capital, lots of small rural dirt tracks with orange-red dirt and plenty of green trees and bushes around.

bw-AwpQ.title: Coverage: paved vs unpaved roads (map)
bw-AwpQ.summary: A map of which covered roads are paved and which are unpaved. Small unpaved side roads in and near towns are not shown.

bw-BrtG.title: Sign: older blue-background road signs
bw-BrtG.summary: Some road signs have a blue background, an older style from before white-background signs. Fairly unique here, though most signs are the newer white ones.

bw-CVOu.title: Landscape: semi-arid hills with short shrubs
bw-CVOu.summary: Many semi-arid hills covered in short shrubs, between the capital and Lobatse in the southeast. Similar hills occur elsewhere and in South Africa, so rule that out first.

differs.how: Similar hills exist across the border

bw-Fm8z.title: Coverage: sparse, densest in the east
bw-Fm8z.summary: Coverage is limited because of few roads. Besides paved roads there are some rural unpaved ones. It is densest in the east and near the capital, and larger towns have many side roads.

bw-GwEW.title: Landscape: very white sand, dry plants
bw-GwEW.summary: A large region in the mid-west has very white sandy soil and dry-looking vegetation. Sandy soil is widespread, so look for the bright white colour.

bw-IGgM.title: Plate: white front, yellow rear
bw-IGgM.summary: UK-style plates: white at the front and yellow at the back. Only Namibia shares this in southern Africa.

bw-OYIt.title: City: richer, developed, mostly flat
bw-OYIt.summary: The capital looks richer and more developed than elsewhere, though some areas are poor. Some southern parts have hills, but most is flat. Only Francistown often looks similar.

bw-Rom4.title: Road: bright yellow fresh lines, dark asphalt
bw-Rom4.summary: Southeast of Tshabong the A20 is freshly repainted with bright yellow lines and dark asphalt, a power line to the northeast, orange-tan sand and patches of yellow flowers.

bw-UxrV.title: Road lines: yellow edges, white centre
bw-UxrV.summary: As across southern Africa, edge lines (if any) are yellow and centre lines white. Israel, Palestine, Jordan and the UAE also have yellow edge lines in dry areas, but they drive on the right.

differs.how: Drives on the right, here on the left

bw-VNqS.title: Landscape: pancake-flat, hills in two areas
bw-VNqS.summary: Most of the country is as flat as a pancake. If you see hills, you are probably in one of the two areas on the minimap, though even there much is flat and some lone hills appear elsewhere.

bw-WC9E.title: Road: construction, service road or embankment
bw-WC9E.summary: The A33 through a forest reserve and wildlife area is under construction, shown by a service road or embankment beside it. Some spots still look normal.

bw-WQ2d.title: Landscape: dry, flat, shrubs, white-to-red sand
bw-WQ2d.summary: Dry and mostly flat, with shrubs, small trees and sometimes dry golden grass. The soil is arid and sandy, from white to red. The South African border region can look similar.

bw-XUN2.title: Road: red-tinted asphalt along the southern
bw-XUN2.summary: The road along the southern border through Middlepits has red-tinted asphalt and arid land, with slight hills in places. Near the town the soil is very red with small white pebbles.

bw-ZP7K.title: Houses: shacks to bungalows, grey bricks
bw-ZP7K.summary: From small shacks to comfortable middle-class bungalows, some with exposed grey bricks and occasionally traditional round huts. Other southern African countries have the same.

bw-b9XY.title: Vegetation: orange autumn trees in straight
bw-b9XY.summary: This part of the A30 feels like autumn, with orange-leaved trees lined up along the road and often tall grass.

bw-d1xZ.title: Sign: green direction signs, A-numbered roads
bw-d1xZ.summary: Green direction signs like the rest of southern Africa. Major roads are numbered with an A, which shows up on direction signs. South African road numbers never start with A.

differs.how: South African road numbers never start with A

bw-eNTS.title: City: bright white sandy soil
bw-eNTS.summary: Maun is the only relatively large city with the bright white sandy soil typical of the mid-western region.

bw-ejAj.title: Chevron: small red-and-white
bw-ejAj.summary: Small red-and-white chevrons are sometimes beside the road. Very common in South Africa too.

bw-fgRE.title: Road: lush trees, tall grass
bw-fgRE.summary: The A33 is greener than usual, with leafy trees and tall grass, and it gets lusher the further north you go.

bw-gr6s.title: Road: power line on the west, grainy asphalt
bw-gr6s.summary: The A35 always has a power line to the west, grainy asphalt with faded markings, and many small tracks running alongside into the bushes.

bw-igGd.title: Landscape: red firm soil
bw-igGd.summary: In the eastern area north of Francistown: red, rocky and firm soil, arid look, trees and bushes with yellow autumn colours, many bare withered trees and some fallen leaves.

bw-jqFy.title: Coverage: winding dirt roads
bw-jqFy.summary: In the far north near the Chobe River: lots of small winding dirt roads with scattered lush bushes, and wildlife such as elephants and warthogs.

bw-jxYh.title: Sign: English, with local-language town names
bw-jxYh.summary: Signs are mostly in English, but town names come from local languages. Afrikaans place names are almost never seen, unlike in South Africa.

differs.how: Afrikaans is common there but almost absent here

bw-leHu.title: Coverage: random small blurs
bw-leHu.summary: Random small blurs, like those on plates and faces, cover odd parts of the picture. Mostly in towns and rarely on rural roads.

bw-lm-163.title: Landscape: dry flat, African plants
bw-lm-163.summary: A dry, flat landscape with African vegetation set back from the road is a good clue. Confirm with a white car back, driving on the left, yellow edge lines and the sun in the north. Eswatini and Lesotho are hilly, and South Africa mostly has a blue car back now.

differs.how: Mostly a blue car back now, not white

bw-lm-489983.title: Pole: generic wooden pole, wooden top
bw-lm-489983.summary: Most poles are plain wooden poles with a wooden top. South Africa uses these too.

bw-lm-80609.title: Phone numbers: 7 digits, 24X is the second city
bw-lm-80609.summary: Local numbers have 7 digits, not 8. A number starting 24X XXXX is from Francistown.

bw-mI5v.title: Landscape: regional soil and plant map
bw-mI5v.summary: An infographic of the main landscape regions, with the soil, vegetation and other clues that set each apart. Click to enlarge.

bw-nG4U.title: Road: clean new asphalt, red soil
bw-nG4U.summary: The A20 has mostly clean, recent asphalt, with some parts much narrower than usual. Red soil, dry grey trees and very little grass.

bw-oPNf.title: Landscape: big hills with bare rock faces
bw-oPNf.summary: A World Heritage site with large hills showing exposed rock faces. All coverage around it is on dirt roads.

bw-p2pn.title: Guardrail: striped curbs and rails
bw-p2pn.summary: Curbs and guardrails are usually striped: black-yellow, red-white or black-white.

bw-qs9y.title: Sign: black-and-yellow striped post
bw-qs9y.summary: A black-and-yellow striped signpost, more rarely red-and-white. In southern Africa only this country has them.

bw-w13P.title: Coverage: salt pans, dirt roads, leafless trees
bw-w13P.summary: Salt pans in the central-east show on the map as lakes. Dirt roads lead to them, with similar soil and grass but many trees. Much was shot in June, so trees are bare or losing leaves.

bw-w9ul.title: Google car: white, no antenna
bw-w9ul.summary: The whole country was covered by a white Google car with no antenna. South Africa, Lesotho and Eswatini have this car too.

bw-wRda.title: Landmark: distinctive silos around town
bw-wRda.summary: Distinctive silos in Pandamatenga in the northeast, visible all around the town.

bw-yo96.title: Road: mostly unpaved, white sand
bw-yo96.summary: The road north of Maun is mostly unpaved, with very white sand and tall green trees. The first paved section has trees, faint markings and power lines on the west.
